title: Signal nightly run-summary v1
description: Written by Signal's orchestrator terminal task to S3 on every run (success and failure). Consumed by Jarvis for monitoring, briefing, and remediation. Treat as an API contract — bump schema_version for breaking changes.

schema_version.description: Increment for any breaking field change. Jarvis's parser gates on this value.

run_date.description: Logical date of the run (YYYY-MM-DD, America/Toronto).

overall_status.description: 'success' = all DAGs succeeded. 'failed' = at least one DAG failed. 'partial' = some skipped/upstream-failed but none explicitly failed.

window_start_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the orchestrator DAG started.

window_end_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the run-summary task ran (end of observable window).

deploy.description: deploy.sh outcome from this boot. Distinguishes a DAG bug from a deploy bug in post-hoc audits. PLUMBING (pre-decided, don't re-litigate): deploy.sh runs at boot BEFORE the scheduler exists, so an Airflow Variable/XCom cannot receive it — nothing is up. deploy.sh writes deploy_status.json to the mounted checkout (exit_status, tier, timestamp_utc, commit_hash); the summary task reads that file. ~3 lines in deploy.sh, Signal-owned (PR-2 territory). v1: this block MAY be null if the status file is absent (deploy.sh predates the writer). v1.1: required once deploy.sh writes it. Jarvis treats null as 'deploy status not yet emitted', not failure.

exit_status.description: Exit code of deploy.sh. 0 = success. Non-zero = deployment failed (DAG runs may be stale or absent).

tier.description: Tier detected by deploy.sh: no-change = boot fetched nothing new, NOTHING deployed (deploy.sh's 'restart'); code-only = new code, scheduler restart; compose-rebuild = full docker compose up --build; migration-applied = SQL migration(s) applied before scheduler start; unknown = fallback. REMEDIATION-CRITICAL (§6.4): Jarvis merges a fix → starts the workbench → deploy.sh should pick it up. If the boot reports 'no-change' when a fix was supposedly merged, the fix did NOT fetch (wrong branch, push failed) and retriggering would re-run the broken code — burning the once-only retry budget on a known failure. 'no-change' vs 'code-only' is how Jarvis verifies the fix landed before retriggering; the two must never be squashed.

commit_hash.description: The origin/main commit deploy.sh reset --hard to. Lets Jarvis tie a run to exact deployed code.

timestamp_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC when deploy.sh finished. Distinguishes a fresh deploy from a stale status file left by a prior boot.

detail.description: Optional free-text from deploy.sh — error message on failure, migration filenames on migration-applied tier, empty on clean code-only runs.

dags.description: One entry per DAG that was triggered (or attempted) by the orchestrator this run.

logical_date.description: Airflow logical date (UTC ISO-8601) for this dag run.

state.description: Final state at the time the run-summary task ran.

wall_clock_seconds.description: Elapsed seconds from DAG run start to end. Null if the run did not complete.

log_excerpt.description: Last N lines of the task log. Jarvis displays the first 3 in a brief; all lines available for escalation context.

rows_written.description: Map of table name → rows PRESENT for run_date (COUNT(*) WHERE date = run_date, not a write-delta — an idempotent re-run reports the same final-state count). ALWAYS carries the fixed table set; the producer runs the same fixed COUNT queries every night, so there is no 'skipped table' case and a key is NEVER omitted. Zero is a measured value, never elided: raw_prices=0 on a successful ingest = market holiday; raw_prices=0 with other failure symptoms = API died — a present zero is exactly the holiday-vs-outage discriminator, and omitting the key would make that anomaly invisible.

data_gates.description: Pass/fail of nightly plausibility checks once the hardening pass lands them. Keyed by check name. Absent until the hardening pass — Jarvis treats a missing data_gates block as 'not yet implemented', not as failure.

detail.description: Human-readable result — threshold, measured value, or failure reason.

quarantine_count.description: Number of tickers quarantined (added to the quarantine set) during this run. A spike here is a data-quality signal worth flagging.

wind_down.description: What the wind-down task OBSERVED at write time — producer-facts only, no consumer inferences. Timeline: the summary is written inside the run; wind-down then async-invokes workbench-stop; the box dies shortly after. So 'completed' (stop actually happened) and 'backstop' (5am kill) are NOT recordable here — the former hasn't happened yet, the latter kills the process that would write it. Jarvis infers those: stop-event present + this summary present = completed; summary absent/truncated by ~6am = backstop night (a first-class alarm, not a field value).

attempted.description: Did the wind-down task reach the point of invoking workbench-stop? False if wind-down was never reached (upstream failure short-circuited the DAG before it).

result.description: The invoke outcome the task observed, written as its final act BEFORE the async invoke returns: 'invoked' = workbench-stop Lambda invoke issued; 'skipped_other_dags_running' = self-check found another tenant DAG active so did not invoke (§5 wind-down ownership); 'invoke_failed' = the invoke call itself raised.

detail.description: Optional free-text — error on invoke_failed, which other DAGs on skipped_other_dags_running, Lambda request-id on invoked.
